[{"id": "nnvMTG5Sl5", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udc65People Manual", "col": 12}}, {"id": "B-CtTCmVDX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The people module contains features relating to the people of the church (i.e. Members, Families, Leadership. etc).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Htx875Wd1w", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The People workspace contains number cards and graphs. The cards count people, members, families and groups, this week's visitations, birthdays and anniversaries, and the members who joined in the last 30 days. The graphs show people added, new members and baptisms. There are also links to various reports (Birthdays, Roles, Letters, etc).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qI9ZNpJJX4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udc64Person", "col": 12}}, {"id": "RZThk3_x4O", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Church people include guests, members, leadership, and other people who interact or are associated with the church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "UJEDTpYJIM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When adding a person, note the following:
- 'Membership' tells how the person is connected to the church: Member, Regular Attender, Visitor or Contact. When you add a 'Membership' life event, Membership changes to Member. If needed, you can create more membership types.
- 'Status' is Active for everyone who still takes part in the church. When someone leaves, set it to Inactive and pick the 'Inactive Reason'. When you add a 'Death' life event, the status changes to Inactive and the reason to Deceased. The person is then left out of the birthday and anniversary reports and cards, the bulletin, the Church Directory, the Rolodex, the Check-In Station and Church Emails. A couple's anniversary is left out when either spouse has died. If needed, you can create more member statuses.
    - Reports, the Church Directory, the Members card and the bulletin count a person as a member only when Membership is Member and Status is Active.
    - The Visitor Log shows new people whose Membership is Visitor or empty.
- Record birth, baptism and other life events in the 'Life Events' table. The 'Birth' event fills 'Birth Date' and 'Age', so you do not type them in. The 'Age' field shows only when the age is known: the birth year is known, and so is the date of death of anyone who has died.
    - When you know only the month and day of a birthday, enter any year in the Date and tick 'Year Unknown'. The birthday still counts, but 'Birth Date' and 'Age' stay blank.
    - A 'Death' event ticks 'Deceased' and fills 'Deceased Date' from the event's date. Both fields show only for a person who has died. The age then stays at the age the person died. It is blank when the date of death is not known.
    - 'Life Stage' is Adult or Child. It comes from the person's 'Household Role' in their family. A person with no household role is an Adult from the age set in People Settings (18 unless you change it), and a Child before that. Life Stage is blank when neither is known.
    - Ages and life stages are brought up to date every night. When a Church Manager changes 'Adult Age' in People Settings, every life stage is checked again a few minutes after saving.
    - Birthdays (This Week) and Birthdays (This Month) list each birthday on its date this year, with the age the person turns in 'Turning'. When the birth year is unknown, the birthday is still listed and 'Turning' is blank. In a year with no February 29, a February 29 birthday is listed on February 28.
    - In the People report, 'Birthday' is blank when the birth year is unknown. In Member Demographics, those members count under Unknown Age.
- If the person has any roles in the church, they should be indicated in the 'Positions' section. 
   - If a position type does not exist, you can create new role types as needed.
- Photos should be added for members. The photos will be used in a member directory in a future versions.
- An email address or phone number may be on one person only, which stops the same person being entered twice. Phone numbers match however they are written, so '(202) 555-0147' and '202.555.0147' are the same number.
    - When two people really use the same one, such as a couple's shared email or a child using a parent's phone, enter it on both people and leave 'Shared From' blank on the owner's row, usually the person who uses it to sign in to the portal. On everyone else's row, set 'Shared From' to the owner: the list offers only the people who already have that email or phone. Any number of people may share one email or phone this way.
    - A family may use a member's email or phone without setting 'Shared From'.
- Email Bounced on an email row shows that email to this address came back. Churchit ticks it when a bounce reaches the church's email account. Church Emails do not send to the address while the box is ticked. Churchit clears the box when you change the address. Untick it yourself when you know that the address works again.
- 'Middle Name' sits between 'First Name' and 'Last Name', and 'Nickname' under 'Full Name'. 'Other Names' is a closed section. Click it to add a Prefix (Mr., Mrs., Dr., Rev.), Suffix (Jr., Sr., II, III, IV) and Previous Last Name (for example a maiden name). When you search for a person in any Person field, the nickname and the previous last name are searched too. 'Display Name' is filled in for you: the nickname (or the first name when there is no nickname), the last name and the suffix, for example \"Bob Smith Jr.\". 'Full Name' stays the first and last name.
- 'Medical Notes' is for health information the church needs to know, such as a condition or a medicine. Only Church Manager, Church Office and Church Check-In Volunteer logins can see it, and only Church Manager and Church Office logins can change it. Other staff logins do not see the field, and members do not see it on their Personal Details page. It is never printed. The Check-In Station shows it to check-in volunteers. Changes to Medical Notes, and to other fields that only some logins can see, do not show in the timeline of the person.
- 'Emergency Contact Name' and 'Emergency Contact Phone' are for someone with no household adult in Churchit, such as a visiting child. The same users who see Medical Notes see them, and the Check-In Station shows them with the medical notes.
- 'Allergies' can also be changed by the member on their Personal Details page. Check-In Settings can print it on name tags, and the Check-In Station shows it.
- 'Source' shows how the person was first added: Desk (typed in on the Person form), Import (by a Data Import), Check-In (added as a New Visitor at the Check-In Station), Connection Card (added from a guest's Connection Card), Portal (added at a first portal sign-in), Sign-Up (added from a guest's sign-up on the Register page) or Form (added from a guest's answer to a form). It is set once and never changes. People added before Churchit recorded this have no Source.
- When the 'Status' is Inactive, pick the 'Inactive Reason' from the list. Add your own reasons, for example Moved away, on the Inactive Reason list. Two reasons are set for you and cannot be deleted or renamed: Deceased (when you add a 'Death' life event) and Transferred to another church (when you confirm a Member Transfer out). 'Inactive Since' is the day the Status changed to Inactive. It is cleared when the person becomes Active again. People who were already Inactive before this was added get the day from the record's history when the history shows the change. Otherwise it stays blank.
- The activity list at the bottom of a Person form shows each time a staff member opened the record, for example \"Jane viewed this\".
- The Connections tab shows the person's records in four groups. Involvement: functions attended, function sign-ups, groups, ministry team assignments, missionaries they belong to and background checks. Care: prayer requests, prayers, visitations, care requests, care assignments, counseling cases and alms requests. Giving: collections, online donations and giving statements. Membership: member transfers. Each one shows only to the roles that can read it, and counts only the records you can open, so another church's records about the person are not counted.
- Letters from this person can be added in the 'Contact' tab
- Tick 'Hide from Directory and Bulletin' to leave a person out of the printed Church Directory, and out of the birthdays and anniversaries in the bulletin. Members can tick it themselves on their Personal Details page in the portal.
- The 'Family' section shows the person's family and marriage. If a family has been selected, the person will be displayed in the \"Family Members\" section on the `Family` form.
- 'Marital Status' is Single, Married, Widowed or Divorced. If needed, you can create more marital statuses. The 'Spouse' and 'Anniversary' fields show only when the person is Married or Widowed.
    - When a Married person gets a spouse, the spouse's document is linked back as Married and the anniversary is shared.
    - When you set a person to Divorced or Single, the marriage ends for both people. The spouse and the anniversary are removed from both, and the former spouse gets the same marital status.
    - A Widowed person keeps the spouse and the anniversary. When you add a 'Death' life event to a married person, their spouse becomes Widowed.
    - When a spouse is added, the couple shares one family. If only one of them has a family, the other joins it. If neither has one, a family named after the person being saved is created, with that person as its primary contact. If they are in different families, no one is moved.
    - A Family can be automatically created from a person by clicking the 'New Family From Person' button. This requires a 'Last Name' to be set, and makes the person the Family's primary contact. The button is there for anyone who is not already the primary contact of a family, so a married son can start his own family.
    - When a married person moves to another family, their spouse moves with them if the spouse was in the same family.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "IqJm62Jfo2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To give a person access to the Church App Portal, the church person must have an associated email address. 
Click the \"Invite to Portal\" button on the 'Person' form to create and associate a new user with the 'Person'. Only users who can change the person can invite them. If a login with that email address already exists, Invite to Portal links it to the person instead. You cannot link a login that another person already has, or a login of a church you cannot see. Linking a staff login, with this button or in the 'Portal User' field, does not change which churches the staff member sees. An administrator sets that in User Permission.
    - The user will be created with 'Church User' permissions and linked with the 'Person' (This should give the user access to their own information as well as information that is shared with them).
    - The user should receive an invitation/welcome email (assuming email settings have been setup correctly).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "staffroles1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Staff logins", "col": 12}}, {"id": "staffroles2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Portal access is for members. Staff and volunteers who work in the desk need a user with a Role Profile that matches their job:
- Church Staff: looks up people, events, groups and ministries, and keeps their own prayer requests, sign-ups and room bookings.
- Church Office: also adds and edits people, families, groups and member transfers.
- Church Care Team: also handles care, counseling, visitation, background checks, and prayer and alms requests.
- Church Treasurer: also handles collections, expenses, funds, budgets and giving statements.
- Church Check-In Volunteer: uses the Check-In Station only.
- Church Manager: everything, including settings.

To give someone several jobs, add more than one Role Profile to their user. Each person only sees the workspaces, reports and dashboards their roles can use.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "twofactor1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Two-factor authentication", "col": 12}}, {"id": "twofactor2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Two-factor authentication asks for a code as well as the password when someone logs in, so a stolen password alone does not open the church's records. We recommend it for every staff login, because staff can see personal and medical details.
To turn it on:
1. Open System Settings and go to the Login tab.
2. Under Two Factor Authentication, tick 'Enable Two Factor Auth'.
3. Choose the 'Two Factor Authentication method': OTP App (a code from an authenticator app on a phone, such as Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator), SMS (set up SMS Settings first) or Email.
4. Save. Each user sets up the method the next time they log in.
When you turn it on, 'Two Factor Authentication' is ticked on the All role, so everyone is asked for a code, members included. To ask only staff, open the All role and untick 'Two Factor Authentication'. Then tick it on the Church Staff, Church Manager and Church Check-In roles. Every staff login holds one of these roles.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "sso_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Single sign-on", "col": 12}}, {"id": "sso_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "With single sign-on, people use one account for Churchit and for other apps. A System Manager sets it up. The Integrations workspace is hidden, so use the links here.
Sign in to Churchit with another account. Use this when your church already has accounts in Google, Keycloak or Authentik.
1. Open Social Login Key. Choose the 'Social Login Provider': Google, Keycloak, or Custom for Authentik and other OpenID Connect providers.
2. Type the 'Client ID' and 'Client Secret' that the other system gives you. For Keycloak, type the address of the realm in 'Base URL'. For Custom, type a one word 'Provider Name', for example authentik, and the 'Authorize URL', 'Access Token URL' and 'API Endpoint' of the other system. Set 'Redirect URL' to /api/method/frappe.integrations.oauth2_logins.custom/authentik.
3. Set 'Sign ups' to Deny. Then only people who have a user in Churchit can sign in. Churchit finds the user from the email address.
4. Tick 'Enable Social Login' and save. In the other system, set the redirect address to your site address followed by the 'Redirect URL' of the key.
The login page then shows a button for the provider.
Use Churchit accounts in another app. Use this for an app that supports OpenID Connect, such as a wiki or Nextcloud.
1. Open OAuth Client. Type the name of the app in 'App Name'.
2. Set 'Scopes' to openid. Type the redirect address that the app gives you in 'Redirect URIs' and in 'Default Redirect URI'.
3. In 'Allowed Roles', add the roles that can use the app. For all staff, add Church Staff, Church Manager and Church Check-In. A user with none of these roles cannot sign in to the app. If you leave it empty, Frappe adds Desk User, so every desk login can use the app.
4. Set 'Token Endpoint Auth Method' to Client Secret Post. The app cannot get a token with Client Secret Basic.
5. Save. In the app, type the 'Client ID', the 'Client Secret' and the discovery address: your site address followed by /.well-known/openid-configuration.
The first time a person signs in to the app, Churchit asks them to allow the app to see their full name, email address, picture and roles.
Other apps can also add themselves as an OAuth Client without a login. If you do not need this, untick 'Enable Dynamic Client Registration' in OAuth Settings.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "grade_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "School grade", "col": 12}}, {"id": "grade_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Type the year that a child finishes high school in 'Graduation Year'. Churchit shows the school grade in 'Grade' and updates it each day. The grade is Kindergarten in the school year that starts 13 years before graduation, then Grade 1 to Grade 12, and then Graduated. Before kindergarten, 'Grade' is empty. The grade goes up on the first day of the month in 'School Year Starts In' in People Settings. The default is August. If your school year starts in January, the school year is the calendar year. When you change the month, the grades change soon after you save. For example, when the school year starts in August, a child with Graduation Year 2030 is in Grade 8 on July 31, 2026 and in Grade 9 on August 1, 2026.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "envelope_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Envelope numbers", "col": 12}}, {"id": "envelope_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "'Envelope Number' on a person is the number on their offering envelopes or the reference on their bank gifts. Two people in one church cannot have the same number. People in different churches can. Type the number in any Person field, for example in a donation row of a collection, to find the person. A signed-in member sees their envelope number on the Give page as the payment reference to use. A People Import file can fill it in with an Envelope Number column. When you merge two people, the person you keep gets the number.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qrcard_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Member QR Card", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qrcard_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Member QR Card print format prints a wallet card for a person. The card shows the church name, the person's name and photo, their Person ID, and a QR code of the Person ID. Open the Person, click the print icon, and select Member QR Card. The card is 3.375 \u00d7 2.125 in, the size of a bank card. At the Check-In Station, click Scan Card and show the card to the camera to find the person and their family.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "skills_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Skills, interests and spiritual gifts", "col": 12}}, {"id": "skills_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Use the 'Skills, Interests and Gifts' field on the Person form to record what the person can do, what they like to do and their spiritual gifts. Select one or more Skills. Each Skill has a category: Skill, Interest or Spiritual Gift. Churchit starts with twelve spiritual gifts from Romans 12, 1 Corinthians 12, Ephesians 4 and 1 Peter 4. Church Managers and People Editors can add more Skills or change them. All churches use the same list of Skills. To find the people with a skill, open the Person list in Report view, add a filter on Skill (Person Skill), and save the report. You can then use it as a smart list (see Lists of People). When you merge two records of one person, the kept person gets the skills of both.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "church_fields_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Church fields", "col": 12}}, {"id": "church_fields_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A System Manager can add the church's own fields to the Person form and the Family form, for example a T-shirt size or a locker number. Do these steps:
1. Open Customize Form and select Person or Family.
2. In the fields table, find the row 'Church Fields' at the end. Add the new field below that row. Do not set 'Mandatory'. Churchit adds people and families without church fields, for example from a Connection Card, an import or My Household, and a mandatory field stops these additions.
3. To show a Person field only to staff with more access, set its 'Perm Level' to 1. Then only Church Managers, People Editors and Check-In users can see it. Do not set a Perm Level on a Family field, because then nobody can see it.
4. Click Update.
The field shows on the Church Fields tab of the form. You can filter a list of people on it and save the list as a smart list. A church field is the same for every church on the site. When you remove the personal data of a person, Churchit clears all of that person's church fields. It also clears the church fields of their family when it clears the family.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "relations_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Relationships to other households", "col": 12}}, {"id": "relations_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Use the 'Relationships' table on the Person form to record a relative or other person who lives in another household, for example a grandparent. Select the Relationship and the Person. You record the relationship on one person only. The other person sees it on their Connections tab, in the Relationships group. Click it to see the people who recorded a relationship with them. You cannot select the person themselves or a person in the same family. Use the Members table of the Family for people in one household. When the directory is private to each church, you can select only people of your churches. When you merge two records of one person, the kept person gets the relationships of both, and a relationship with themselves is removed. When you remove the personal data of a person, or delete a person, Churchit removes all relationships that other people have with them. When you remove the personal data, Churchit also removes the relationships on that person.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "merge_person_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Merge two records of one person", "col": 12}}, {"id": "merge_person_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When one person has two records, merge them. Open the record you do not want to keep, click \u22ef > Merge Into\u2026, select the person to keep and click Merge. Only users who can delete people, such as a Church Manager, can merge, because a merge deletes a record.
- Everything that names the removed record moves to the kept record: attendance, giving, groups, ministry teams, care, prayers, comments, attachments and the history of changes.
- The kept record keeps its own values, except the values that you choose from the removed record (see below). Each empty field gets the value of the removed record. A spouse comes with the Marital Status of the removed record.
- The emails, phone numbers, addresses, life events, positions, letters, skills and relationships of the removed record are added to the kept record. A value that the kept record has already is not added again, and the primary email, phone and address of the kept record stay primary.
- The portal login moves to the kept record when the kept record has none.
- A list that names a person once, such as the members of a group, the attendance of a function or the members of a family, keeps one row for the person.
- The kept person stays in their own family. A kept person with no family joins the family of the removed record.
- A Possible Duplicate for the two records is marked Merged.
- When both records came from an import, the kept record keeps its own Imported ID. A comment on the kept record names the other ID. The next import from that system adds that record again, so merge the two in that system too.
- The removed record is deleted for good. It is not kept in Deleted Documents.
Churchit does not merge two people when both have a portal login, when they have different spouses, when they are married to each other, or when they belong to different churches. You cannot undo a merge. The Rename dialog's 'Merge with existing' follows the same rules. You cannot change the ID of a person in any other way.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "merge_choice_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Choose the value to keep. When both people have a value for a detail and the values are different, the merge dialog shows a table. Each row is one detail, and each column is one person. Select the value to keep in each row. The person you keep has their own value selected by default. Details that only one person has go to the person you keep automatically. You can choose only the details that you can edit. A Portal User or an Envelope Number that the other person still has cannot move in a merge. To give it to the person you keep, clear it on the other person first, and then set it on the person you keep.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "forget_person_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Remove the personal data of a person", "col": 12}}, {"id": "forget_person_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Church Manager or a System Manager can remove the personal data of a person who asks the church to forget them. Open the person and click \u22ef > Remove Personal Data. The record stays with the name Anonymized, so their giving and attendance still count in reports.
- Churchit removes the name, emails, phone numbers, addresses, letters, photo, medical notes, emergency contact, allergies, anniversary, skills, how they heard of the church, church fields, portal login and Imported ID. The Gender becomes Unknown, and the person is hidden from the directory.
- The Birth life event is removed. The other life events keep their type and date, so the counts for each year stay correct, but they lose their location and notes.
- The person leaves their family and their spouse. The spouse keeps their own Marital Status. Churchit removes the relationships on the person and the relationships that other people have with the person. A family with no members left is anonymized too. A family that keeps members loses the person's first name from its name, so \"Smith - John\" becomes \"Smith\".
- Records that name the person keep the link, but the name and email address of the person are removed from their titles and text.
- The history of changes, the comments and the attachments of the record are deleted, and so are those of the records about the person, such as background checks, care requests, counseling cases and giving statements. Emails and texts sent to the person lose their address and text, but a Church Email still counts them as sent. The follow-up actions that failed for the person lose their error message.
- The person's open Follow-up Cards are closed. Their Card Closed actions do not run, and no other workflow starts from them.
- The person's answers on each function sign-up are deleted, and the answers of the other people on the sign-up stay. The name, email and phone they typed on their own sign-ups are removed, also on a guest sign-up made with one of their email addresses that was never linked to them.
- The person's Person Notes, Connection Cards and Form Responses are deleted, and so are the Pickup Restrictions that protect them as a child.
You cannot undo this. The portal login is disabled. When a member asks for their data to be deleted and a System Manager approves the Personal Data Deletion Request, Churchit removes the personal data of their record in the same way.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "retention_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Remove personal data on a schedule. In People Settings, set 'Remove Personal Data After (Years Inactive)' to the number of years. Once each day, Churchit then removes the personal data of people who have been Inactive for that number of years or more. It removes the same data as Remove Personal Data and adds a comment to the person that gives the reason. It does up to 50 people each day, the people who became Inactive first. People who have died are kept. 0, the default, never removes data. The Personal Data Due for Removal report shows who is next and the Removal Date of each person. Only Church Managers and System Managers see this report. To keep the data of a person, set their Status back to Active before that date.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "TZBrYvFWti", "type": "header", "data": {"text": "Visitations", "col": 12}}, {"id": "SJPiHfoARN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Visitations are visit of a person by a church representative. 
When adding a visitation, note the following:
-  The visitation type can be changed, or new visitation types can be added.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "notes_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Person Notes", "col": 12}}, {"id": "notes_b1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Person Notes keep what staff know about a person, for example a phone call, a visit or something to remember. To add one, open the person, click \u22ef at the top and choose Add Person Note. Pick a Category, write the note and save. You stay on the person's form. The Date is today unless you change it. When the note records a call or a visit, pick how you were in touch in Contact.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "notes_b2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A person's notes show in the Activity list at the bottom of their form, on the day each note records. Tick Pinned to keep a note at the top. Tick Alert to show the note in red at the top of the person's form, for example \"Hard of hearing. Face him when you speak.\" Only people who may read the note see the alert.
You see only the notes your role may read. Other notes do not show in the Activity list, in the Person Note list or in reports. Notes cannot be shared with other users.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "notecat_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Note Categories", "col": 12}}, {"id": "notecat_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Note Category decides who reads and adds its notes. A Church Manager sets the categories up. If you have more than one church, every church uses the same categories. Only a Church Manager of the main church can add or delete a category, or change its roles or Private. A branch can still change the Description.
- Roles That Read Notes: the roles that can read notes in this category. Leave it blank to let all staff read them.
- Roles That Add Notes: the roles that can add and change notes in this category. Leave it blank to let all staff add them.
- Private: only the person who wrote a note can read it. A Church Manager cannot read it either.
Churchit starts with three categories. Every staff member reads General. Only the care team and Church Managers read Pastoral Care and Benevolence. Benevolence holds the case notes of alms requests. The text from a person's old Notes field is now a note in General. If a role can add notes in a category but cannot read them, its users cannot open a note again after they save it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A37CU_rUFj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udc68\u200d\ud83d\udc69\u200d\ud83d\udc67\u200d\ud83d\udc66Family", "col": 12}}, {"id": "_wxytNqTX4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Families are groups of people who are related.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qQr_8PsoeH", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When adding a family, note the following:
- After adding a family, you may want to link people to the family. When a person is linked to a family, that person will be displayed in the \"Family Members\" list.
- Set the 'Primary Contact' to the family member the family is named after. You can pick only a person in the \"Family Members\" list.
- On a site with more than one church, a family belongs to the church of its 'Primary Contact'. You can make someone the primary contact only when you can see their church. In the same way, you can put a person into a family of another church, from the Person form or the Family form, only when you can see both churches.
- In the \"Family Members\" list, the 'Relationship to Primary Contact' of each member tells what they are to the primary contact, such as Wife or Son. The primary contact's own row tells what they are in the family, such as Husband.
    - The primary contact and their spouse are labelled Husband and Wife from the 'Spouse' field on the person. No other member can be Husband or Wife.
    - A member's spouse who has no relationship yet gets one from the member: a Son's wife is a Daughter-in-law, a Daughter's husband is a Son-in-law, and a Brother's wife is a Sister-in-law.
- When you change the 'Primary Contact', the family is renamed after the new primary contact, such as 'Doe - John' to 'Doe - Jane'. Each relationship changes to the relationship to the new primary contact, so the mother of the old primary contact becomes the Mother-in-law of the new one. Filter by Group Type or by Group.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0a0Yfbfao3", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcd4 Church Directory", "col": 12}}, {"id": "aIL5EgTGiJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To generate a Church Directory:
1. Navigate to People > Church Directory
2. Select which options you want for the report. They are in groups, and the directory preview is updated after each selection:
    - People:
        - Members Only: This will filter out any non-members from the directory.
        - Hide Non Active People: This leaves out everyone whose Status is not Active, with their birthday and their anniversary. A couple is left off the anniversaries when either person is not Active. A family whose primary contact is not Active is listed by its surname only. This option is off by default.
        - Group by Family: This will list each family together under the family name, with the primary contact first, then their spouse, then the other members by name. When it is off, each person is listed by name.
        - People with 'Hide from Directory and Bulletin' ticked are always left out, with their birthday and their anniversary. A family whose primary contact is hidden is listed by its surname only, such as 'Doe Family' for 'Doe - John'. A family whose members are all hidden is left out.
        - People who have a 'Death' life event are always left out too, with their birthday, and so is a couple's anniversary when either spouse has died. A family whose primary contact has died is listed by its surname only.
    - Show:
        - Photos: This will display available photos in the directory.
        - Positions: This will show the person's church position under their name in the directory
        - Membership: This will show how the person is connected to the church, such as Member or Visitor, next to their name.
        - Family Relationships: This will show each person's 'Relationship to Primary Contact' from their Family, such as Husband, Wife or Son. When it is off, no relationships are printed.
    - Contact Details:
        - Phone Numbers: This will show each person's primary phone number.
        - Emails: This will show each person's primary email address, and the email address of each missionary.
        - Addresses: This will show each family's primary address. A family member whose own primary address is different shows it under their name. A person without a family, and every person when Group by Family is off, shows their own primary address, or their family's when they have none.
    - Extra Pages:
        - Birthday List: This will include a list of all the people's birthdays near the end of the directory.
        - Anniversary List: This will include a list of people's anniversaries near the end of the directory. Each couple is listed by their own names, such as 'John & Mary Smith'.
        - Missionaries: This will include a list of missionaries at the end of the directory, with the names of the people in each missionary's People table. Missionaries whose Status is Inactive are left out. If the missionary is marked as 'sensitive', only the name, people, photo, and agency will be shown. A person in a listed missionary's People table is left out of the family and individual pages, so they are not shown twice.
        - Notes Page: This will add a lined page at the end of the directory for handwritten notes.
    - Groups:
        - Group List: This will include a list of the groups at the end of the directory, with each group's name and description. Groups whose Status is Inactive are left out.
        - Group Members: This will list the members of each group that has 'Show in Directory' ticked, by first name, several to a line. People that the directory leaves out, such as hidden people, are left out of the groups too. This option shows when Group List is ticked.
        - Member Roles: This will show each member's Group Role next to their name, such as 'John Smith | Leader'. This option shows when Group Members is ticked.
    - Printing:
        - Church Image on Cover: This will show the church's image, such as a logo, at the bottom of the cover. The image fills the width of the page, or the space under the text when it is tall. Set the image on the Church record.
        - Page Numbers: This will number each page in its outer bottom corner. The cover is not numbered.
        - Booklet: This will make the PDF a half-size booklet. Each side of a letter sheet holds two pages, in the order that lets you fold the stack in half. The cover is on the front and the back cover is always blank, so the Blank Back Cover option is hidden. A booklet needs a multiple of four pages, so up to three extra Notes pages are added at the end. The last Notes page stays just inside the back cover.
        - Blank Back Cover: This will add an empty last page, so the back of the directory stays blank.
3. Click 'Print Directory' to open the directory as a PDF, then print it from there. For a booklet, print double-sided and flip on the short edge. - Type in the search box to find a name, family, phone number or email address.
- Tap a letter down the side, or drag your finger along the letters, to jump through the alphabet.
- Use the buttons on the front of a card to call, text, email or map the person.
- Tap a card to turn it over. The back shows their positions, groups, birthday and age (the month and day only when the birth year is unknown), anniversary, membership and address, with an Open link to their record.
- Switch to Households to see one card per family. People without a family keep a card of their own.
- Click Filters to narrow the cards by membership, status, group or position, and by church when your site has more than one. - Your saved cards stay with your login, so a list built on a computer is waiting on your phone.
- From the tray you can Email everyone saved (their addresses go in BCC, so no one sees the others), Print their cards, or Add to Group if you can edit groups. Clear empties the tray.
- Save all, Email all and Print above the cards work on everyone your search and filters are showing.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "map_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\uddfa\ufe0fMap of Addresses", "col": 12}}, {"id": "map_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Click Map of Addresses in the People sidebar to see the addresses on a map. - When you add an address, or change its Address Line 1, City/Town, State/Province, Postal Code or Country, Churchit sends that text to the OpenStreetMap search service (Nominatim). It sends no name. Latitude and Longitude on the address then fill in, usually within a few seconds.
- If the service cannot find the address, Latitude and Longitude stay 0 and the address is not on the map. Correct the address and save it again.
- Churchit sends one address each second. After the update that added the map, the addresses already on file fill in one by one. This can take some time.
- The map shows only the addresses on the current page of the list. To see more, click 100 or 500 at the bottom.
- To keep every address on this site, clear 'Look Up Addresses for the Map' in People Settings. Nothing is sent while it is clear, and addresses not on the map yet stay off it. - To use a different Nominatim server, open Geolocation Settings, set Provider to Nomatim and set Base URL to the server's address.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mt_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udce8Member Transfers", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mt_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Member Transfers record people transferring into or out of the church.
- Set the Direction (In/Out), the other church, and update the Status as the transfer progresses.
- When you confirm a transfer Out to a church that is not one of your branches, the person's Membership changes to Contact, their Status to Inactive, and their 'Inactive Reason' to Transferred to another church. The Member Transfer keeps the name of the other church.
- When you confirm a transfer In, the person gets a 'Membership' life event dated that day, which names the other church. Their Membership changes to Member and their Status to Active. Nothing changes for a person who is already an active member.
- A 'Letter of Transfer' can be printed from the form.
- With multi-church on, a move between your own branches is a transfer with a To Church: confirming it moves the person (and their portal access) to that branch.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mc_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcc8Membership Changes", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mc_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit keeps a record each time a person is added and each time their Membership or Status changes. The Membership Changes report lists these changes for a date range, the last 90 days unless you change it. Each row shows the date, the person, the field, the value before the change and the new value. Use the Field and New Value filters to find, for example, everyone who became a Member this year. Changes made before this report was added come from each person's change history.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "funnel_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83e\ude9cAssimilation Funnel", "col": 12}}, {"id": "funnel_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Assimilation Funnel report shows how far new people go after their first visit. Set 'First Visit From' and 'First Visit To'. The default is the last 3 months. The report lists each living person whose first attended function is between these dates. For each person it shows four steps:
- First Visit: every person in the list.
- Came Back: the person attended a function again within the number of weeks in 'Came Back Within (Weeks)'. The default is 8.
- Connected: the person is in a group or has served on a ministry team.
- Member: the person's Membership changed to Member between the first date and today.
A person can get to a step without the step before it. The numbers at the top and the chart show how many people got to each step.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pathway_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udee4\ufe0fPathways", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pathway_b1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Pathway is a path people take through the life of the church, for example Came Back, Joined a Group, Baptized and Serving. Each step is a smart list: a saved Report Builder list of people or a saved Attendance Count. A person has done a step when they are on the step's list.
To make a pathway, first save a smart list for each step, for example a list of people whose Groups count is 1 or more. Then add a Pathway, give it a name, and add one row for each step, in the usual order. In Smart List, pick the step's list.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pathway_b2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Click Open Progress on the pathway, or open the Pathway Progress report and pick the pathway. The report lists each living person who has done at least one step, with a tick for each step done, the number of steps done, and the first step that is not done yet. A person can do a later step before an earlier one. The numbers at the top and the chart show how many people have done each step. With more than one church, a pathway counts only the people of its own church.
To start a follow-up when a person reaches a step, add an On Smart List trigger with the step's list to a Follow-up Workflow.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lists_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udccbLists of People", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lists_fields", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Connections tab of the Person form shows figures that Churchit keeps up to date from other records, so you can filter people on them:
- Involvement: First Attended, Last Attended and Times Attended (90 Days) come from function attendance that is Confirmed, Assumed or Checked-In. Last Served and Times Served (90 Days) come from accepted ministry team assignments. Groups and Group Count show the groups the person is in. A group with the status Inactive does not count.
- Giving: First Gift and Last Gift come from donations on submitted collections, paid online gifts included. Lapsed Giver is ticked when the last gift was more than 90 days ago but within the last year. Only Church Finance, Church Manager and System Manager users see these fields or can filter on them.
- Care: Open Care Requests counts the care requests that are not Resolved or Closed. Last Visited is the latest completed visit. Background Check and Background Check Expires show the most recent check, and a cleared check past its expiry date shows as Expired. Only Church Pastoral Care, Church Manager and System Manager users see these fields or can filter on them.
The figures change soon after a record is saved, and again every night. They count only the records of the person's own church and the records shared with all churches. On the Person form, users see the Giving and Care figures only for people of a church they can see. In lists, reports and exports they can still see them for people of every church while the directory is shared (see the Foundations manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "engagement_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Engagement. The Connections tab of a Person also shows how the person takes part in the church. The Activity chart shows the functions that the person attended on each day of the last year. A darker square shows more functions on that day. The chart shows only the functions that you can see. Under the chart, Stats shows First Attended, Last Attended, Times Attended (90 Days), Groups and Last Served. Times Attended (90 Days) and Groups are green when the person has some and orange when they have none. If you can see the Giving fields, Stats also shows Last Gift. Last Gift is orange when the person is a Lapsed Giver.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lists_standard", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Standard lists. A standard list is a saved list of people that stays up to date by itself. Open one from the People sidebar under Person Reports, or from the People workspace:
- Inactivity Candidates: active people who attended before but not in the last 90 days.
- First-Time Visitors: people who first attended in the last 30 days.
- Not in a Group: active adults who are in no group.
- Children: all children.
- Background Checks Expiring: cleared background checks that expire in the next 30 days. Only pastoral care staff and managers see this list.
- Lapsed Givers: people who gave in the last year but not in the last 90 days. Only finance staff and managers see this list.
- People with Open Care Requests: people with a care request that is not resolved or closed.
- Members Not Seen Lately: active members who attended before but not in the last 90 days, least recently visited first.
- Members by Last Visit: active members, starting with those never visited, then those visited longest ago.
Only pastoral care staff and managers see these three lists.
No list shows people who have died. You cannot change a standard list. To keep your own version, change the filters or columns, then click Save As.
The Inactivity Candidates and First-Time Visitors cards on the People workspace count the people on each list in your church. Click a card to open the list. On a site with more than one church, a list shows the people of every church unless Keep People and Families Private to Each Church is on. When you open it from the card, it shows only your church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lists_own", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Make your own list. Open the Person Report view. Click Filter and add conditions, for example Status is Active and Times Attended (90 Days) is 0. To change the columns, use \u22ef > Pick Columns. Then click \u22ef > Save As and type a name. You need the Church Manager role to save a list.
A saved list is open to every staff role that can read people. To limit who sees it, open it from the Report list and change the Roles table. To open a saved list again, pick it under Saved Reports in the Person Report view.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lists_email", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Get a list by email. A Church Manager opens the list, clicks \u22ef > Setup Auto Email, and adds an Auto Email Report. Set User to the person whose access the email uses, then set Email To, Frequency (Daily, Weekdays, Weekly or Monthly) and Format. Keep Send only if there is any data ticked, so no email is sent when the list is empty. The email shows only the people that user may see.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lists_team_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Lists by team, membership date and life event", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lists_team_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each person has these fields. Churchit fills them in, and you cannot change them on the form.
- Ministry Teams: the ministries that have a team position that lists the person. An Inactive ministry is not shown.
- Team Positions: the team positions that list the person. The positions of an Inactive ministry are not shown.
- Membership Changed On: the date that the Membership last changed.
- Status Changed On: the date that the Status last changed.
To make a list, open the Person Report view and add a filter. For example:
- People on the Welcome team: add the filter Ministry Teams (Person Ministry Team) Ministry equals Welcome.
- People who became members in 2025: add the filter Membership equals Member, and the filter Membership Changed On between 1 January 2025 and 31 December 2025.
- People baptized in 2025: add the filter Life Event (Life Event) Event Type equals Baptism, and the filter Life Event Date between 1 January 2025 and 31 December 2025.
Save the report to use it as a smart list. The teams and team positions of a person show only the positions of the person's own church and shared ministries. Each person who can read the directory can see the teams and team positions of a person.
Churchit updates these fields some seconds after a change. A daily job also updates all of them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lists_count_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Attendance count lists", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lists_count_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Open the Attendance Count report. Set Since to the first date to count. Set At Least (Times) to the number of times a person must attend. You can also set Until and a Function Type. The report counts only attendance that is Confirmed, Assumed or Checked-In, and only on functions that have started. It counts only the functions of the person's own church and shared functions. It leaves out people who have died. To use the report as a smart list, open the menu at the top right, click Save, and give the list a name. The saved list then shows in the Smart List field of a Church Email, a Pathway step, and an On Smart List trigger of a Follow-up Workflow. A saved list keeps its filters and counts again each time it is used. A saved copy of another script report is not a smart list.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lists_act_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Acting on a list", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lists_act", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Tick people in the Person list or in a saved list, then open Actions:
- New Church Email starts a draft Church Email to the people you ticked and opens it, so you can write it and send it. You see it only if you can send Church Emails.
- Email opens an email with their addresses in BCC, so no one sees the others. Churchit leaves out people who do not allow email, and tells you who they are and who has no email address.
- Email Household Adults emails the Adults of their households, for example the parents of a list of children. Each address is used once. An Adult who does not allow email is left out, and Churchit tells you who.
- Open in Rolodex shows only the people you ticked. Click Picked in the list to see everyone again.
- Add to Group adds them to a group. You see it only if you can edit groups.
- Mark Inactive sets Status to Inactive with the Inactive Reason you pick, and Inactive Since to today. People who are already Inactive keep their reason. You see it only if you can edit people.
- Add Tags tags them, and Filter > Tags finds them again.
In the Family list, Actions > Email emails each household at its own email address, or at its primary contact's when it has none.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lists_labels_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Mailing labels", "col": 12}}, {"id": "lists_labels", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Tick people or families, then click Actions > Print. Pick Mailing Label in the Person list, or Household Label in the Family list (addressed like \"John & Jane Smith\"). Each label prints on its own 3.5 x 1.125 inch page, for a roll label printer such as a DYMO LabelWriter (30252 labels) or a Brother QL (DK-1201 labels).
A person with no address of their own gets their family's address. The country prints only when it is not your church's country.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "clean_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83e\uddf9Clean Data", "col": 12}}, {"id": "dup_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Possible Duplicates", "col": 12}}, {"id": "dup_b1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When you add a person, Churchit compares the name, email and phone with the people already in the directory. If the new person may already be there, a yellow note shows at the top of the form. The note gives a link to each person and the reasons. The note does not stop you from saving.
Each week, Churchit looks for people in the same church who may be the same person. It adds each pair to the Possible Duplicates list. It does not pair people in the same family. It does not add a pair again after someone closes it. An import adds pairs for the people it adds.
The Possible Duplicates card on the People workspace shows how many pairs are open. Open a pair to see the two people side by side. A gray row has the same value for both people.
- Click Merge to make the two people one person, then select the person to keep. See 'Merge two records of one person' above. Only users who can delete people see Merge.
- Click Not a Duplicate when the two people are different people. Churchit does not pair them again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "dup_b2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit gives each pair a score from 0 to 100. The same email, phone, birth date and name make the score higher. A different first name, birth date, gender or suffix (for example Jr. and Sr.) makes the score lower. Churchit knows common nicknames, so Bob and Robert can be the same person. A pair must reach the Duplicate Match Threshold in People Settings. The default is 80. A higher number finds fewer pairs.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "find_contact_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Find a person by phone or email", "col": 12}}, {"id": "find_contact_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In a field where you select a person, you can type a first, middle or last name, a nickname, a phone number or an email address. Type four or more digits of the phone number, in any format. Type the email address with its @ sign.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "quality_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "People Data Quality report", "col": 12}}, {"id": "quality_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The People Data Quality report shows living people whose records need attention. Each row shows one problem and, when it helps, the value to fix. The problems are: No Way to Reach (no email, phone or address on the person or on their family), Invalid Email, Invalid Phone Number, Email Bounced, Mail Returned, Possible Duplicate, Child Without Birth Date and No Family. Use the Problem filter to see one problem at a time.
When mail sent to an address comes back, tick Mail Returned on that address row of the person. Mailing labels then leave that address out.
When email sent to an address comes back, Churchit ticks Email Bounced on that email row. Church Emails then do not send to that address. Ask the person for a new address. When you change the address, Churchit clears Email Bounced. You can also untick it yourself.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "import_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udce5Import People", "col": 12}}, {"id": "import_b1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "You can add people from another church system or from a spreadsheet. Churchit uses Frappe's Data Import tool. Data Import reads the file, shows a preview, and adds the people in the background. Church Managers and System Managers can import people. A Church Manager sees only the Data Imports they made.
Each row of the file is one person. Churchit makes a Person for each row and a Family for each household. The people of one household share one Family and its address.
Churchit keeps the ID that each person and household had in the old system. When you import a newer file from the same system, Churchit updates these people. It does not add them again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "import_pco_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Import from Planning Center", "col": 12}}, {"id": "import_pco_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. In Planning Center People, open the gear menu and click Import & Export CSV.
2. Click Start Export. Planning Center sends you an email with a link. Download the CSV file. If the download is a ZIP file, open it and use the CSV file in it.
3. In Churchit, in the People sidebar, click Data Imports, then click Add Data Import. Set Document Type to Planning Center Import.
4. For the first import, keep Import Type as Insert New Records. For a later import, select Insert or Update Records.
5. Save, upload the CSV file and click Next. Do not change the file. Churchit reads the Planning Center columns as they are.
6. Map each value that Churchit does not know to a value of your church, or skip its rows. For example, map the Name Prefix \"Mr.\" to \"Mr\".
7. Click Import.
Household Primary Contact sets the Primary Contact of the Family. A person with Child set is a Child of the household. The other people of the household are Adults.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "import_rock_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Import from Rock RMS", "col": 12}}, {"id": "import_rock_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Rock RMS cannot export all people at once. Make a report one time. Then export it to Excel each time you import.
1. In Rock, open Tools, then Reports, and add a report for the Person entity.
2. Add the fields below to the report. For each field, set Column Header to the name in this list: Id, Family Id (the Primary Family Id field), Family Name, Family Role (the Age Classification field), Title, First Name, Nick Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Suffix, Gender, Birthdate, Anniversary Date, Marital Status, Connection Status, Record Status, Inactive Reason, Is Deceased, Email, Mobile Phone, Home Phone, Work Phone, Home Address Street 1, Home Address Street 2, Home Address City, Home Address State, Home Address Postal Code, Home Address Country. You must add Id, Family Id and First Name. The other fields are optional.
3. Run the report and click Export to Excel.
4. In Churchit, in the People sidebar, click Data Imports, then click Add Data Import. Set Document Type to Rock RMS Import.
5. For the first import, keep Import Type as Insert New Records. For a later import, select Insert or Update Records.
6. Save, upload the Excel file and click Next.
7. Map each value that Churchit does not know. For example, map the Connection Status Attendee to Regular Attender, and the Record Status Pending to Active.
8. Click Import.
Rock has no head of household. Churchit makes the first Adult of each family in the file its Primary Contact. You can change the Primary Contact on the Family.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "import_breeze_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Import from Breeze", "col": 12}}, {"id": "import_breeze_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. In Breeze (Tithely ChMS), click the gear icon to open Account Settings. Click Manage Account, then View More, then Export.
2. Select People and click Export. Download the spreadsheet.
3. In Churchit, in the People sidebar, click Data Imports, then click Add Data Import. Set Document Type to Breeze Import.
4. For the first import, keep Import Type as Insert New Records. For a later import, select Insert or Update Records.
5. Save, upload the file and click Next. Do not change the file. Churchit reads the Breeze columns as they are. Make sure that the Birthdate column uses the date format mm/dd/yyyy. If it does not, change the date format of that column before you import.
6. Map each Status that Churchit does not know to a Membership, for example Attender to Regular Attender, or skip its rows.
7. Click Import.
People with the same Family value share one Family. The Head of Household is the Primary Contact, and the Family gets their name. A family with no Head of Household gets its first Adult as Primary Contact. A person with the Family Role Child is a Child of the household. A Spouse or an Adult is an Adult. For Unassigned, Churchit sets no role. A person with a known birth date at or over the 'Adult Age' becomes an Other Adult. Set the other roles on the Family.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "import_sheet_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Import from a spreadsheet", "col": 12}}, {"id": "import_sheet_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. In the People sidebar, click Data Imports, then click Add Data Import. Set Document Type to People Import, save, and click Download Template to get the columns.
2. Put one person on each row. Give each person a Person ID. Give the people of one household the same Household ID. Set Primary Contact to Yes for one person of each household. Set Household Role to Adult, Other Adult or Child.
3. If the people come from another system, type its name in Imported From. Otherwise leave it blank.
4. Upload the file, look at the preview, and click Import.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "import_after_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The preview and after the import", "col": 12}}, {"id": "import_after_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A row that cannot be imported stops the import, for example a row with no first name. Correct the file, or click Skip Row. A value that Churchit does not know stops the import until you map it or skip its rows. A note does not stop the import. For example, a note tells you which Person a row updates, or that an email address is not valid and Churchit leaves it out.
The import log shows the Person that each row added or updated. Each imported Person has the Source Import. Imported From and Imported ID show where the person came from.
To remove what an import added, see Undo an import below.
An update changes only the fields that have a value in the file. It adds new email addresses, phone numbers and addresses. It does not remove the old ones.
Churchit compares each new person with the people already in Churchit. If two people may be the same person, Churchit adds a Possible Duplicate. Review each Possible Duplicate and merge the people that are the same.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "import_undo_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Undo an import", "col": 12}}, {"id": "import_undo_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "You can remove the people and families that one import added, for example after an import with wrong columns. Do it soon after the import, before people add attendance, gifts or notes to the new records. You need the right to delete people and families, which a Church Manager has.
1. Open the Person list and click Filter. Add 'Source' equals Import, 'Imported From' equals the system, for example Planning Center, and 'Created On' between the day of the import and the same day. For a spreadsheet import with no Imported From, use only Source and Created On.
2. Make sure that the list shows all the people. If it does not, click 500 at the bottom of the list.
3. Tick the box in the list header to select all the people. Click Actions > Delete, and then click Delete.
4. Open the Family list. Filter on 'Imported From' and 'Created On' in the same way. Select all the families and delete them in the same way.
What happens:
- Churchit removes each deleted person from their family and from the record of their spouse. It also deletes the Possible Duplicates of the person and the relationships that other people recorded with the person. When a person who stays shares the phone number or email address of a deleted person, the person who stays keeps the phone number or email address.
- Frappe does not delete a person that a later record names, for example a person who attended a function after the import. It shows the records that it did not delete. Keep these people, or delete the later records first.
- Frappe does not delete a family that still has a person, so the families of the people who stay also stay.
- When you delete more than 10 records, Frappe deletes them in the background and shows a message when it is finished.
The undo removes only the people and families that the import added. It does not change back the people that an Insert or Update Records import updated. The addresses of the deleted families stay in the Address list. A System Manager can delete them there.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "conn_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\ude4bConnection Cards", "col": 12}}, {"id": "conn_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Connection Card is the welcome card a guest fills in on their phone, at /connection-card on your website. They tell you their name, email and phone, whether they are new, and what they would like to do next. After a guest sends a card, Churchit looks for them in the directory.
- If one person has the same email or phone and the same first and last name, the card is linked to that person, and Churchit does not change that person's details.
- If not, Churchit adds the guest as a new person with the membership Visitor. Any close matches go to Possible Duplicates for you to check.
- Then each follow-up workflow that starts on a Connection Card opens a follow-up card for the person.
The Connection Card list shows every card, with its status, its person and when it was processed. A Church Manager can also add a card in the desk from a paper card, and Churchit processes it the same way.
When a Connection Card adds a new person, the person's 'How They Heard' field gets the answer that the guest gave on the card. When the card is linked to a person who is already in the directory, Churchit does not change that person's 'How They Heard'. You can also type it on the Person form.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "conn_qr_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Print a QR code for the form", "col": 12}}, {"id": "conn_qr_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Open the Connection Card web form and click QR Code. If you have more than one church, pick the church that the cards are for. A guest who scans that code sends their card to that church. Leave Church empty for the main church. Click Download to save the code as an image for your bulletin or welcome card. Every published web form has this button, so you can do the same for the prayer request form.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "conn_int_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What guests can tick", "col": 12}}, {"id": "conn_int_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The boxes under \"I Would Like To\" come from the Connection Card Interest list. Churchit starts you with Join a group, Serve on a team, Learn about baptism, Learn about membership and Talk with a pastor. You can rename them, delete them or add your own. To start a follow-up workflow when a guest ticks one, add a Connection Card trigger to the workflow with that interest in Which. A Connection Card trigger with no value starts on every card.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "conn_household_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Who came with the guest", "col": 12}}, {"id": "conn_household_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In Who Is With You? a guest can add the people who came with them: first name, last name, relationship and birth date. When Churchit adds a new Visitor for the guest, it also makes a Family with the guest as the Primary Contact. It adds each person from the list as a Visitor in that Family, with the relationship the guest chose. A person with no last name gets the last name of the guest. A Wife or Husband becomes the spouse of the guest. A birth date becomes a Birth life event, so the Family can set the household role. People who look like someone on file go to Possible Duplicates. If the card matched a person who is already on file, Churchit adds nobody from the list, because a card never changes a person on file. The list stays on the card; add these people by hand if you need them. A card marked Spam adds nobody.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "conn_spam_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Spam and busy Sundays", "col": 12}}, {"id": "conn_spam_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The form has a box that people never see. Robots fill it in. A card with that box filled in gets the status Spam and nothing else happens; the sender is not told. If a real guest's card was marked Spam, add the person yourself.
Each internet address can send the form at most 10 times a minute. On a busy Sunday, guests on the church Wi-Fi share one address. A guest who sees a \"too many requests\" message can send the card again a minute later.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fu_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83e\uddedFollow-up", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fu_wf_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Follow-up Workflows", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fu_wf_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Follow-up Workflow is a list of steps that you use to look after a person, for example Welcome Call, Coffee Invitation and Connect to a Group. Add a workflow and give it a name. Add one row for each step, in order. In Assign To, choose who takes the step. In Due In (Days), say how many days they have to finish it. A step with no user is not assigned to anyone. The person in Assign To must be able to see your church's records.
When you save the workflow, Churchit makes a board for it, with one column for each step. Click Open Board to see it. If you change the steps, the board changes the next time you save. You cannot remove a step while open cards are on it. Move those cards first.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fu_card_h", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Follow-up Cards and the board", "col": 12}}, {"id": "fu_card_b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A Follow-up Card is one person on one workflow. It shows the person's phone number and email address, the step it is at, and when it is due. A person can have only one open card on a workflow. To add a card by hand, open the person, go to Connections and click + next to Follow-up Card.
To move a card, drag it to the next column on the board, or open the card and click Move To. When a card moves, the person for the new step gets a to-do and one email, and the due date starts again from the new step.
